description: Level 1 (Dusty Hollow): 3 blasts, 2 surveys, and 3 contract attempts with no vehicle ever bought -- named for an efficient $80k win, but no hauling infrastructure means no delivery ever succeeds; see Findings #54-#57 for the real trajectory asserted instead, and for confirmation (via an inspected screenshot, not just source reading) that the survey confidence overlay this file was originally written to gate on now genuinely renders -- the stale 'FAILS until GameRenderer wires survey overlay into syncFromContext()' warning this file previously carried is no longer true.

expect.note: Findings #54-#57: this file's original `employee assign_skill 1 geology 3` used the same rejected positional syntax as Finding #45 -- fixed to `skill:geology level:3`, which matters more here than in other files since this file's whole premise is the survey confidence overlay, and `SurveyCalc.ts` confirms surveyor skill level directly reduces estimate noise (Finding #54). The 2 contract-accept steps in the file's first contract cycle both click the same unqualified `.bs-contract-accept` selector -- the Contracts panel has no per-row selector, so each click lands on whichever contract is currently first-listed; with the original hardcoded `contract accept 1`/`contract accept 2` text, command mode would accept only 1 contract (the first attempt failing outright) while a real click-driven run would accept 2 (each click hits a different, now-shifted first row) -- a genuine, dangerous activeContractCount divergence between modes, not just a wrong-number typo. Fixed by deriving both real target IDs from a direct trace and pairing the command text to what each successive click actually lands on. Discovered mid-fix that correcting the `assign_skill` syntax shifted the RNG stream far enough (better survey noise draws feeding the shared Random instance) to change which contract IDs were even available by the time contract cycles ran, requiring a full re-trace rather than reusing an earlier one (Finding #55). Same Finding #52 class recurred a 3rd time: all 3 of this file's `drill_plan grid` steps declared spacing/depth the real Drill panel never used (no stepper-click interaction step sets them), so the real drag-to-grid formula produced substantially bigger grids than declared (16/25/36 holes vs. the declared 9/16/16) -- fixed the same way, by matching the declared grid to what the real drag at the panel's true defaults produces. The corrected, much larger 3rd blast (36 holes vs. the originally-declared 16) is violent enough to kill both of the 2 employees hired immediately beforehand, taking deathCount from 1 to 3 -- a real, reproducible consequence of the fix, not a scenario bug (Finding #40's exact precedent) (Finding #56). Like the 2 previous playthrough files, no vehicle is ever bought, so despite 3 real blasts every contract delivery fails honestly for lack of storage -- not re-fixed here for the same reason as `level1-win-conservative.json` (the mechanism is already proven end-to-end by `level1-playthrough-win.json`). Verified the file's own stated premise directly rather than trusting its stale warning: inspected `screenshots/scenario-level1-win-efficient-interaction/step-31-survey.png` (a real browser run) with the Read tool and confirmed the survey confidence overlay genuinely renders (a lime tile-pattern coverage overlay on the terrain) and the Results panel shows real computed confidence (96% for the core sample, 89% for the seismic survey) -- the file's original 'FAILS until GameRenderer wires survey overlay into syncFromContext()' warning is stale; that wiring already exists in current `GameRenderer.syncFromContext()` (Finding #57). No bankruptcy, revolt, or ecological shutdown -- cash ends at $46,760 despite $50k in penalties/costs, thanks to two lucky_strike random events landing on +$10,000 each (both reproduced identically in the real browser run). safety and nuisance both bottom out at exactly 0 by the end from the accumulated real blast violence. Verified in both command mode and a real interaction-mode run with screenshots (83/83 steps, 0 failures).
